slides.headline: Tungsten tiles survived 74 plasma blasts in DIII-D
slides.sub: Full-size divertor tiles made via PBF-EB endured four minutes of high-confinement plasma exposure during a three-day campaign at the DIII-D fusion device. Melting point: 3,422°C.

slides.headline: PBF-EB tungsten divertor tile pair installed in DIII-D
Manufacturing: PBF-EB on JEOL JAM-5200EBM
bullets: Tiles produced using Electron Beam Powder Bed Fusion (PBF-EB)
JEOL, NC State, and ORNL collaborated on the manufacturing
Each tile pair measures 136 x 143 mm, 20 mm thick
Wire EDM shaped mounting features on each tile

slides.headline: Surface finishing: CNC grinding with digital twin
bullets: Multi-axis CNC grinder programmed with a digital twin of the tile
Removed approximately 250 microns from the plasma-facing surface
Resulted in a gently domed surface with ~1 m radius
Mounting features on copper-alloy pedestals

slides.headline: OpenAI's AI Found 948 Linux Privilege Escalation Exploits
slides.sub: In a 30-hour run, a cyber-focused AI model identified 2,308 candidate vulnerabilities, dynamically reproduced 1,724, and generated working local privilege escalation (LPE) exploits for a commonly used Linux distribution.

slides.headline: The Pipeline in Action
slides.caption: Server racks at a data center. The pipeline scanned approximately 2.8 million lines of Linux kernel code.

slides.headline: 4-Stage Pipeline Architecture
bullets: Vulnerability discovery — scans kernel code for weaknesses
Dynamic validation — reproduces vulnerabilities in real environments
Exploitability assessment — determines if LPE is feasible
Patch generation — creates remediation code

slides.headline: Key Findings & Costs
bullets: Scan covered ~2.8 million lines of kernel code
Agents discovered 10+ novel Linux exploitation techniques
Total cost: ~$1.2M in API credits
~$1,279 per LPE exploit generated

slides.headline: The Stated Warning
slides.quote: "For the near and medium term, having access to a low-privileged account on an operating system that isn't up-to-date on its latest available patches should be considered functionally equivalent to root access for a well-resourced threat actor."

slides.headline: What This Means
bullets: Bad actors can use the same AI to weaponize zero-days
The pool of viable targets expands with minimal effort
No GitHub or kernel documentation was involved
No review or confirmation by Linux maintainers occurred

slides.headline: The Bottom Line
slides.sub: AI-driven vulnerability research is no longer theoretical. A single pipeline run generated nearly 1,000 working exploits in 30 hours. The question is no longer whether AI can find vulnerabilities — it's how quickly adversaries can deploy them before patches land.

slides.headline: 6 rules against cognitive surrender
slides.sub: AI-generated code silently erodes your engineering judgment. Here's how to keep agency.

slides.headline: Gather domain knowledge before implementation
slides.sub: Understand data shapes, missing patterns, field-specific libraries and existing implementations before writing code.
slides.name: arxiv

slides.headline: Distinguish problem framing from coding
slides.sub: Separate programmatic framing (decomposition, abstractions, architecture) from mechanical translation into syntax.
slides.name: arxiv

slides.headline: Choose appropriate AI interaction models
slides.sub: Use conversational tools for architecture, IDE assistants for completion/refactoring, and autonomous agents for rapid prototyping.
slides.name: arxiv

slides.headline: Think through a potential solution first
slides.sub: Specify inputs, expected outputs, constraints, edge cases and how the solution fits the broader architecture before prompting.
slides.name: arxiv

slides.headline: Manage context strategically
slides.sub: Provide all necessary information upfront, restat critical requirements in long conversations, and use externally-managed context files.
slides.name: arxiv

slides.headline: Implement test-driven development
slides.sub: Frame tests as behavioral specifications before requesting implementation, providing concrete test cases and using AI for edge cases.
